# Phase Two — Architecture and File Map

The Awtsmoos gives each boundary a vessel and each vessel a name;
Awtsmoos.com should let calendar, Torah text, and road-read meet without tangling the frame.

## Candidate architecture to test against the repository

A. Calendar-first resolver: date -> Hebrew date -> weekly sedra -> weekday -> aliyah range.
B. Data-first resolver: canonical annual calendar table -> date key -> sedra/aliyah metadata.
C. Provider-first resolver: trusted external daily-Chitas endpoint -> normalized local grouping.
D. Hybrid resolver: local Hebrew calendar/parsha calculation + canonical aliyah boundaries from existing Torah metadata.
E. Heichel-native resolver: use an existing grouping/progression plugin if road-read already supports computed groups.

## Preferred shape if the code supports it

Choose D + E: keep the Heichel UI generic, add a small pure Chitas calendar domain layer, and feed its result into the existing grouping abstraction.

## Expected responsibilities

- `calendar`: determine Jewish date and relevant weekly sedra in selected Israel/diaspora mode.
- `parsha`: map sedra names/identifiers to seven aliyah boundaries.
- `chitas`: map weekday to the corresponding daily Chumash span.
- `adapter`: translate the Chitas span into the road-read grouping schema.
- `tests`: verify ordinary weeks, double parshiyos, festival displacement, year boundary, Israel/diaspora divergence, and Sunday-to-Shabbos sequence.

## Files to touch

Unknown until tracing is complete. The final plan will enumerate exact observed paths only. No speculative source path will be created merely because this document names a responsibility.

## Constraints

- Complete-file writes only.
- New modules should be small and focused.
- No runtime scraping if a deterministic local calculation is feasible.
- Existing Heichel routing/grouping conventions win over a new custom UI.
- Chumash text should come from the project’s existing Torah source where possible.
- A date calculation must make timezone/location policy explicit instead of relying on ambient browser UTC.
